title: The purpose and workings of a vector database

videos.script: So far every search in this course has been one line of NumPy. Multiply the question by every stored vector, and sort. {{numpy}} That line is exact, and it is the yardstick for everything after it. This lesson asks what it costs and what it lacks. {{question}} First the cost. You will time it over ten thousand, a hundred thousand and a million vectors. The time grows with the count, because every query reads every vector. {{brute}} Then what it lacks. A NumPy array has no ids, no metadata, no way to change one record, and it is gone when the program stops. {{missing}} You will write the smallest store that has those things, in about fifty lines. A collection with one model and one dimension, fixed when it is created. Records made of an id, a vector, metadata and the text. {{store}} You will update a record and delete one, and see that a delete leaves a tombstone until the store is compacted. {{tombstone}} And you will follow one question down the whole path: embed it, search, filter, fetch the text. On this machine, most of the time goes on the first step. {{path}} Every vector database in the next three lessons does these same things, at a scale this one never will. {{end}}
